$schema_note: Per-type stat/formation/growth dials for the typed unit model. Decisions + rationale live in docs/design/squad-group-system.md §1/§2/§4. All values are PROTOTYPE DIALS (first pass, unmeasured) — same status as economy.json and squads.json. types.spearmen.melee_subtypes (added task-088) is the melee identity split — see docs/design/retinue-melee-subtypes.md for the decision, row count, and the ten-silhouette-to-row mapping.
note: Records the SHIPPED CVAR DEFAULTS this spec proposes (Swarm.Formation.<Type>.*, Swarm.<Type>Combat.* — CVar names to be finalized by whoever implements task-046), the same role squads.json already plays for allocation dials. Not a runtime-read table; CVars stay the live source of truth so these remain tunable while the game runs, per SwarmFormation.h's own stated reasoning.

spearmen.note: Mechanically today's retinue, renamed and formalized as a type. Stats are the shipped Gate 1 defaults, unchanged (docs/GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3b 'shipped defaults').

stance_reflavor.follow: escort at FollowEngageRange, engage what comes close

melee_subtypes.note: DECIDED task-088, 2026-07-30 — docs/design/retinue-melee-subtypes.md. Each row REPLACES the combat block above for units rendered as its mapped silhouette(s); formation, stance_reflavor, and growth_source_weight are unchanged and shared by every row (only the combat stat block varies per row — GDD §10 Mass Entity data-cheap-soldier constraint). Derived from docs/data/scenarios/retinue-subtypes.json's task-094 ten-way candidate profiles (sim-director-owned candidate data, NOT copied verbatim): solo rows are that file's primary-formula combat block rounded to whole numbers; line_standard/line_light are the arithmetic mean of their two merged silhouettes' combat blocks, rounded the same way. min_engage_range (0) and move_speed_scale (1.0) are uniform across all 9 rows — no measured shape axis in the source formula feeds either one. variant_to_row is KEYED BY ATLAS INDEX (0-10, docs/data/art/team-variants.json's variants[].index / SwarmSheet::Team — task-095 reads the index, not the silhouette name); the name is carried alongside purely for readability and must not be treated as the binding key. heavycloak/simplecolumn's targets_per_hit respecced 9/10 -> 8, task-099 (Swarm.*TargetsPerHit accessors clamp 1..8, SwarmCombatProcessors.cpp:253-260) -- see per-row notes and docs/design/retinue-melee-subtypes.md.

retinue_base.note: Atlas index 0, task-085 (landed after this decision was first drafted) — the pre-split shipped look, ~20% of the army at default Swarm.TeamVariantWeights. NOT derived from the shape formula; it has no measured silhouette in retinue-subtypes.json. Ships as spearmen's existing combat block unchanged (Gate 1 defaults) so it reads as the baseline, not as an eleventh knight sub-type.

heavycloak.note: targets_per_hit respecced 9 -> 8, task-099: the shipped combat loop's nearest-target array is fixed at 1..8 (SwarmCombatProcessors.cpp:253-260) and was already silently clamping this row's raw formula value to 8 in play. 8 is the nearest legal value to the formula's derived rank, not an invented number, and matches what task-095 already ships. Identity carries on max_hp instead (165 is the highest of all 9 rows) -- see docs/design/retinue-melee-subtypes.md Ceiling reconciliation.

shieldbreak.note: Formula reads this silhouette's high asymmetry as high-DPS, not the 'more HP, less DPS' defensive guess task-086's brief made at a glance — resolved toward the formula (see design doc): 'shieldbreak' itself is an offensive name, not a defensive one.

bracedstaff.note: Sits 4.8-5.9% from line_standard (v4_overhead) in every task-094 run — a flagged near-miss, roughly double the gap of the two pairs actually merged below. Kept as its own row: the gap is at the low end of 'clearly separated', not inside the collapsed band, and merging it would span three consecutive ranks (5/6/7) on evidence that only measured 5-vs-6 and 6-vs-7 pairwise, not 5-vs-7 directly.

line_standard.note: v4_overhead + v11_midguard merged — 1.8-2.4% apart in every task-094 run (2 scenarios, 5 seeds), the tightest pair measured. combat block is the arithmetic mean of the two silhouettes' primary-formula stats. The holes-driven 'two-handed' alt-hypothesis probe for v4_overhead (retinue-subtypes.json's v4_overhead_holes_swap) was NOT adopted — it's an explicit probe, not a shipped candidate, and moot for the stat block now that this row is shared; the two-handed read is preserved as a visual/animation identity only.

simplecolumn.note: targets_per_hit respecced 10 -> 8, task-099: same 1..8 combat-loop ceiling as heavycloak (SwarmCombatProcessors.cpp:253-260), already silently clamping this row in play. 8 is the nearest legal value to the formula's derived rank. Identity carries on engage_range/dps instead (82 is the shortest engage_range of all 9 rows, tied-lowest dps at 28) -- retinue-subtypes.json's own v6_simplecolumn derivation note already flagged its nominal cleave as mostly unreachable at this engage_range, independent of this ceiling. See docs/design/retinue-melee-subtypes.md Ceiling reconciliation.

line_light.note: v7_barestance + v1_narrowguard merged — 3.3-3.8% apart in every task-094 run, second-tightest pair. combat block is the arithmetic mean of the two silhouettes' primary-formula stats; targets_per_hit's mean (8.5) rounds DOWN to 8, not up to 9 — this is the bottom-tier row by every other stat and rounding up would drift it toward simplecolumn/line_standard's band for no reason the data gives.

archers.note: New in this revision. UNMEASURED — needs the same zero-input-baseline treatment GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3 gave the original retinue tuning before these numbers should be trusted for balance.

stance_reflavor.follow: hold formation, engage anything inside EngageRange without closing distance
stance_reflavor.charge: Volley Advance (rate/cleave bump, not movement — never closes to melee)
stance_reflavor.hold: Loose from Cover (anchors identically to Follow; value is in addressing one unit)
stance_reflavor.rally: Fall Back (collapses behind the nearest Spearmen unit if one exists, else the hero)

adaptation.note: DECIDED 2026-08-08 (owner). Evolution ladders. Decision home docs/design/adaptation.md; columns docs/data/unit-types.schema.md v0.2; art mapping docs/art/adaptation-roster.md. A rung is the triple (unit_type, tier, variant_index). 'tier' keys upgrades.json tier_ladder.tiers[] -- THE STAT SPINE, deliberately not restated here, so no HP/DPS number appears anywhere in this block. 'variant_index' is the team-units.json atlas index, the same binding key melee_subtypes.variant_to_row[].index uses. RANK IS rungs[] ARRAY ORDER, never variant_index -- atlas order is arbitrary-by-history and frozen (Scripts/art/atlas.py:306-309). Every index below resolves to a row that ALREADY EXISTS in the 24-row team atlas, so Adaptation adds zero repack debt: py Scripts/art/atlas.py check --all must stay byte-identical. All values are PROTOTYPE DIALS (first pass, unmeasured) except where a note says CITED or MEASURED.
adaptation.handle_rule: One command handle per BRANCH, not per rung -- a branch is a type under GDD.md Q29/D14, a rung is a look-and-stat move inside a type. A captain plus its retinue is ONE handle, not one per body. Four branches below = four handles. NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN C++ TODAY: EUnitType is one bit (SwarmFragments.h:266), all 8 handles are consumed at the shipped RetinueCap 128, D14 itself is unimplemented, and a unit's look is recomputed every frame from spawn phase with nowhere to store an assigned variant (SwarmFragments.h:406-423). adaptation.md sec.6 carries the full list; filed as its own task.
adaptation.separation_measured_note: MEASURED 2026-08-08, the tier axis only: py Scripts/sim/sweep.py adaptation-ladder --axis "scenario:Retinue.Composition[UnitType=spearmen].Tier=freed,militia,veteran,bannerman" gives freed 6.75s -> militia 2.70s -> veteran 1.42s (60.0% and 47.4% separation against docs/sim/SUBTYPE-VARIETY.md:401-403's 5.4% floor) -> bannerman 2.08s, SLOWER. The captain inversion is CORRECT, not a defect: bannerman is 160/35 against veteran's 190/45 and its value is an aura the point-target model has no primitive for. Do not raise its stats to flatten the table. The SILHOUETTE axis is measured separately per branch below.

ladders.families_note: Two family folders, ONE body group -- both descend from PixelLab character 1c935515 / group 2cc3ab61, which is why this reads as one ladder rather than two. adaptation.md sec.8's 'one family's axis' rule is satisfied at the body-group level, not the folder level; recorded here because the folder split is an artefact of when the states were generated, not a design boundary.
ladders.single_branch_note: Deliberately one branch. The ten knight looks never fork into distinct registers -- per knight-melee-v1/v2's own axis notes they are all one sword-and-shield identity. Seven unused looks (v2/v4/v6/v7/v10/v11/v13) could seed a reach/polearm second branch later; brief in docs/art/adaptation-roster.md, NOT built.
ladders.separation_note: CITED from docs/sim/SUBTYPE-VARIETY.md (task-094)'s own ten-way ranking: militia -> veteran 60.8% gap, veteran -> bannerman 6.9% gap, both clearing that doc's cited 5.4% floor. Monotonic in the derived max_hp bulk proxy 114.5 -> 139.9 -> 164.5.

rungs.note: The pre-split shipped look. Carries no melee_subtypes row at all (task-088 addendum), which is why it has no bulk proxy -- qualitatively the unarmed baseline, not a measured rung.

rungs.captain_grammar: bulk -- the single largest/heaviest look in the branch
rungs.retinue_note: Escort wears the MILITIA rung's own look, so a captain visibly commands soldiers of its own gear tier rather than the base freed look.
rungs.retinue_size_note: JUDGMENT CALL -- 8 is half TypeLegibilityCeiling (SwarmSubsystem.h:59). No measurement in this project gives a captain retinue size; the ceiling is the only legibility number it owns.
rungs.upkeep_note: OPEN (O7) -- whether captain retinue draws Supply upkeep was never put to the owner. Explicit null, not a guess.

shop.price_note: OPEN (O8), blocked on O4 -- gold's drop rate and sources are undecided (GDD.md Q26). Pricing before that is invention.
shop.stock_rule: Offers rungs on branches the player's pick did not grant.
shop.captain_note: The bannerman rung is NOT purchasable -- upgrades.json's own trait says 'item/event reward only, not a purchasable tier'. Captains are earned; everything below them is buyable.

ladders.shared_freed_note: All three archer branches share variant_index 11 as their freed rung -- one base archer look before the kit register diverges. This is also what makes the atlas budget work: 3 branches cost 10 rows, not 12.
ladders.separation_note: WEAKEST LADDER OF THE FOUR, flagged rather than smoothed, with the exact margins pinned so nobody has to re-derive how thin they are. bbox 2162 (ghilliecloak) -> 2256 (+4.3%, stoutbeard) -> 2116 (-6.2%, hollowmask); opaque 1152 -> 1178 (+2.3%) -> 1090 (-7.5%). Both axes swing under ~6% and the bannerman rung goes DOWN on both. The three looks ARE three visibly different soldiers -- a ghillie cloak, a squat bearded build, a hollow mask -- but the separation is in pathfinder-line's own stated kit/headgear axis (family.json separation_rationale), which none of the four scalar silhouette measures can see. QUALITATIVE, NOT MEASURED. This does not block the ladder; it blocks a FUTURE claim that this branch is sim-validated the way spearmen-line is. Precedent for accepting a visual verdict over a metric: broken-machine/family.json checks_run[], where a visual pass correctly overruled the better-measuring pair.

rungs.captain_grammar: salience -- highest-contrast/most-enclosed look, a 'point of glow' leader marker rather than the biggest body
rungs.retinue_note: Archer escorts reuse the shared FREED look, unlike spearmen. Archers have no per-branch equivalent of 'escort wears the militia look' because each archer branch's militia rung is branch-specific and distinct.

shop.stock_rule: Offers rungs on branches the player's pick did not grant.
shop.captain_note: bannerman rung not purchasable -- see spearmen-line.

ladders.separation_note: Escalates on FOOTPRINT and reach while opaque mass FALLS: bbox 2116 -> 2438 (+15.2%) -> 2650 (+8.7%), opaque 1239 -> 1033 (-16.6%) -> 927 (-10.3%). Flagged, not smoothed over -- the ladder reads as a unit getting longer and more mechanical rather than bulkier, which is coherent for a gun register but means bulk is the WRONG proxy to judge this branch by.

shop.stock_rule: Offers rungs on branches the player's pick did not grant.
shop.captain_note: bannerman rung not purchasable -- see spearmen-line.

ladders.separation_note: Strongest archer ladder BY MEASUREMENT through the veteran rung: bbox 1794 (carbinesuit) -> 2116 (+18.0%, rocketshoulder) -> 2650 (+25.3%, turretnest), opaque 874 -> 1045 (+19.6%) -> 1269 (+21.4%), every delta clearing the 5.4% floor by a wide margin. NOTE THE RUNG ORDER CHANGED 2026-08-08: those figures are the pre-swap ladder, when turretnest was the top rung. Post-swap the top two are transposed, so the branch now reads carbinesuit -> turretnest -> rocketshoulder and the final step DROPS ~20% on both axes. The three looks still separate by exactly the same margins -- only their order changed -- but this branch can no longer be cited as monotonic. See the bannerman rung's captain_flag.

rungs.note: DEMOTED from bannerman 2026-08-08. It is the single biggest silhouette in the whole archer block, which is exactly why it was the first pick -- but it is a seated ground emplacement, and furniture does not lead a moving retinue. Reads correctly as a heavy veteran emplacement.

rungs.captain_grammar: pose -- a standing, striding soldier shouldering a dramatic weapon, i.e. it reads as an INDIVIDUAL rather than as the largest object
rungs.captain_flag: SOFTEST OF THE THREE CAPTAIN GRAMMARS. 'Dramatic weapon' is a weaker leadership tell than spearmen-line's raw bulk or archer-scout's lit-marker contrast. Promoted 2026-08-08 after turretnest was rejected; it is the best look ON DISK, not the right look. TRADE ACCEPTED AND STATED: the swap costs this branch its monotonic growth at the top rung -- veteran -> bannerman now DROPS ~20% on both footprint and mass instead of climbing. That is tolerated for the same reason the captain rung is exempt from the TTK monotonicity gate (adaptation.md sec.9): a captain is a role, not a bigger number. NAMED GAP, not a solved problem -- a purpose-generated 'gunnery sergeant, standing, pointing the retinue forward' look would beat this pick outright and is the one piece of new art this system actually wants.

shop.stock_rule: Offers rungs on branches the player's pick did not grant.
shop.captain_note: bannerman rung not purchasable -- see spearmen-line.

adaptation.unassigned_looks_note: Named, not forced. Spearmen: 7 unused looks (indices 2/4/5/6/8/9/10) could seed a reach/polearm second branch. Archers: 3 unused (v2_bowextended, crystalstaff, arcbow) do NOT cohere into a fourth register on their own -- two arcane-ish looks is not a 3-rung branch. Briefs in docs/art/adaptation-roster.md; no art generated.
adaptation.duplicate_constraint_note: No two rungs on one ladder may be byte-identical twins. 13 byte-identical groups exist on disk and no tool in this repo compares sprites across families (adaptation.md sec.8). Checked: neither known duplicate group intersects the 14 distinct indices used above.

allocation.unit_claim_order_note: Spearmen claim their fair share of MaxSquads (docs/data/squads.json squad_manager.max_squads) first; Archers get the remainder. See squads.json squad_manager.typed_allocation for the formula this feeds.

ranged_combat_model.note: Minimum viable model (spec §2): reuses the existing StrikeReachSq/BlowsClaimed grid mechanism with a larger EngageRange. min_engage_range per type is the only line-of-fire mitigation — an approximation (archers won't target anything already in melee range of anyone), not true LOS. The volley visual is a render-only cue (an arc/trail on SwingBit), out of this file's scope — a performance-director / render-bridge ask, not a sim mechanic.
